tools.name: hollow_box
tools.description:
Builds the six faces (one block thick) of a region: walls, floor and ceiling. The interior becomes air unless keepInterior is true. Typical first step for a room or house body; cut doors and windows afterwards with place_block or clear. Optional onlyReplace: list of blocks; only cells currently holding one of them are changed (a bare id matches every state of that block, "minecraft:air" = only empty cells).

Coordinates are integer block positions in the build (Y up; north = -Z, south = +Z, east = +X, west = -X). Regions are inclusive boxes between two corners given in any order. Blocks are Java Edition blockstates ("minecraft:oak_planks", "minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=east,half=top]"); the namespace is optional, omitted properties take their defaults, unknown blocks or properties are rejected with suggestions.

Examples:
- Room 7×5×7 with planks walls and empty inside: {"region":{"from":{"x":0,"y":1,"z":0},"to":{"x":6,"y":5,"z":6}},"block":"minecraft:oak_planks"}

tools.name: wall
tools.description:
Builds a vertical wall, one block thick, along the horizontal line from (from.x, from.z) to (to.x, to.z) (inclusive; diagonal lines use Bresenham), from layer from.y up to from.y + height - 1. to.y must equal from.y. Optional onlyReplace: list of blocks; only cells currently holding one of them are changed (a bare id matches every state of that block, "minecraft:air" = only empty cells).

Coordinates are integer block positions in the build (Y up; north = -Z, south = +Z, east = +X, west = -X). Regions are inclusive boxes between two corners given in any order. Blocks are Java Edition blockstates ("minecraft:oak_planks", "minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=east,half=top]"); the namespace is optional, omitted properties take their defaults, unknown blocks or properties are rejected with suggestions.

Examples:
- Wall along X, 10 long and 4 high: {"from":{"x":0,"y":1,"z":0},"to":{"x":9,"y":1,"z":0},"height":4,"block":"minecraft:bricks"}

from.description: Start of the wall base line; its y is the bottom layer.

to.description: End of the wall base line; y must equal from.y.

height.description: Number of layers, counted upwards from from.y (>= 1).

block.description: Java Edition blockstate, e.g. "minecraft:stone_bricks" or "minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=east,half=top]". Namespace optional; omitted properties take their defaults.

items.description: Java Edition blockstate, e.g. "minecraft:stone_bricks" or "minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=east,half=top]". Namespace optional; omitted properties take their defaults.

onlyReplace.description: Mask: only cells currently holding one of these blocks are changed (patterns as in `replace.from`, `minecraft:air` allowed). Omit to change every cell. At most 16 items.

tools.name: floor
tools.description:
Places one horizontal layer at height y over the X/Z footprint of region (the region's Y values are ignored). Optional onlyReplace: list of blocks; only cells currently holding one of them are changed (a bare id matches every state of that block, "minecraft:air" = only empty cells).

Coordinates are integer block positions in the build (Y up; north = -Z, south = +Z, east = +X, west = -X). Regions are inclusive boxes between two corners given in any order. Blocks are Java Edition blockstates ("minecraft:oak_planks", "minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=east,half=top]"); the namespace is optional, omitted properties take their defaults, unknown blocks or properties are rejected with suggestions.

Examples:
- Plank floor at y = 1: {"region":{"from":{"x":1,"y":0,"z":1},"to":{"x":7,"y":0,"z":5}},"y":1,"block":"minecraft:spruce_planks"}

region.description: Only the X/Z footprint is used; its Y is ignored.

from.description: Block position, integers in [-4096, 4096]. Y is up; north = -Z, south = +Z, east = +X, west = -X.

to.description: Block position, integers in [-4096, 4096]. Y is up; north = -Z, south = +Z, east = +X, west = -X.

y.description: Height of the single layer. Range -4096..4096.

block.description: Java Edition blockstate, e.g. "minecraft:stone_bricks" or "minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=east,half=top]". Namespace optional; omitted properties take their defaults.

tools.name: place_block
tools.description:
Places a single block at pos (overwrites what is there). Use for details: doors (place the lower half; the upper half "half=upper" separately), torches, windows, furniture.

Coordinates are integer block positions in the build (Y up; north = -Z, south = +Z, east = +X, west = -X). Regions are inclusive boxes between two corners given in any order. Blocks are Java Edition blockstates ("minecraft:oak_planks", "minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=east,half=top]"); the namespace is optional, omitted properties take their defaults, unknown blocks or properties are rejected with suggestions.

Examples:
- Door facing south: {"pos":{"x":3,"y":1,"z":6},"block":"minecraft:oak_door[facing=south,half=lower]"}

pos.description: Block position, integers in [-4096, 4096]. Y is up; north = -Z, south = +Z, east = +X, west = -X.

block.description: Java Edition blockstate, e.g. "minecraft:stone_bricks" or "minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=east,half=top]". Namespace optional; omitted properties take their defaults.

tools.name: replace
tools.description:
Replaces blocks inside region: every cell matching "from" becomes "to". "from" is a pattern: a bare id ("minecraft:oak_stairs") matches every state of that block, written properties must match. Properties not written in "to" are copied from the replaced block where "to" supports them (so replacing oak_stairs by spruce_stairs keeps orientation); remaining ones take defaults.

Coordinates are integer block positions in the build (Y up; north = -Z, south = +Z, east = +X, west = -X). Regions are inclusive boxes between two corners given in any order. Blocks are Java Edition blockstates ("minecraft:oak_planks", "minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=east,half=top]"); the namespace is optional, omitted properties take their defaults, unknown blocks or properties are rejected with suggestions.

Examples:
- Swap all oak stairs for spruce stairs, keeping their orientation: {"region":{"from":{"x":0,"y":0,"z":0},"to":{"x":10,"y":10,"z":10}},"from":"minecraft:oak_stairs","to":"minecraft:spruce_stairs"}

to.description: Block position, integers in [-4096, 4096]. Y is up; north = -Z, south = +Z, east = +X, west = -X.

from.description: Pattern: a bare id matches every state of that block; listed properties must match.

to.description: Replacement. Properties not written here are kept from the replaced block when valid.

tools.name: clear
tools.description:
Sets every cell of region to air (removes blocks). Use to cut doors and windows.

Coordinates are integer block positions in the build (Y up; north = -Z, south = +Z, east = +X, west = -X). Regions are inclusive boxes between two corners given in any order. Blocks are Java Edition blockstates ("minecraft:oak_planks", "minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=east,half=top]"); the namespace is optional, omitted properties take their defaults, unknown blocks or properties are rejected with suggestions.

Examples:
- Door opening 1×2: {"region":{"from":{"x":3,"y":1,"z":0},"to":{"x":3,"y":2,"z":0}}}

tools.name: mirror
tools.description:
Mirrors the content of region in place: axis "x" flips east/west (X coordinates), axis "z" flips north/south (Z coordinates). Blockstates are mirrored too (stairs, doors, logs …). All cells of the region are rewritten, including air.

Coordinates are integer block positions in the build (Y up; north = -Z, south = +Z, east = +X, west = -X). Regions are inclusive boxes between two corners given in any order. Blocks are Java Edition blockstates ("minecraft:oak_planks", "minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=east,half=top]"); the namespace is optional, omitted properties take their defaults, unknown blocks or properties are rejected with suggestions.

Examples:
- Flip a wing east/west: {"region":{"from":{"x":0,"y":0,"z":0},"to":{"x":4,"y":6,"z":8}},"axis":"x"}

from.description: Block position, integers in [-4096, 4096]. Y is up; north = -Z, south = +Z, east = +X, west = -X.

to.description: Block position, integers in [-4096, 4096]. Y is up; north = -Z, south = +Z, east = +X, west = -X.

axis.description: x: flip east/west (X coordinates). z: flip north/south (Z coordinates).

tools.name: rotate
tools.description:
Rotates the content of region clockwise (seen from above) by turns × 90° around the vertical axis, blockstates included. The result is anchored at the region's minimum corner; for 1 or 3 turns the X and Z sizes swap (a 5 wide (X) × 3 deep (Z) footprint becomes 3 wide × 5 deep). Source cells not covered by the result become air; cells covered by the result are overwritten (including with air).

Coordinates are integer block positions in the build (Y up; north = -Z, south = +Z, east = +X, west = -X). Regions are inclusive boxes between two corners given in any order. Blocks are Java Edition blockstates ("minecraft:oak_planks", "minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=east,half=top]"); the namespace is optional, omitted properties take their defaults, unknown blocks or properties are rejected with suggestions.

Examples:
- Turn a 5×3 porch by 90°: {"region":{"from":{"x":0,"y":0,"z":0},"to":{"x":4,"y":3,"z":2}},"turns":1}

region.description: Inclusive box between two corner cells (any order).

from.description: Block position, integers in [-4096, 4096]. Y is up; north = -Z, south = +Z, east = +X, west = -X.

to.description: Block position, integers in [-4096, 4096]. Y is up; north = -Z, south = +Z, east = +X, west = -X.

turns.description: Clockwise quarter turns seen from above (1 = 90°, 2 = 180°, 3 = 270°).

tools.name: copy
tools.description:
Copies the content of region (including air) so that the region's minimum corner lands at "to"; with repeat n, copy i (0-based) lands at to + i × step (step defaults to {x: region size along X, y: 0, z: 0}). The source is read before anything is written, so overlapping copies are safe; copies overwrite the destination. Use for rows of windows, columns, fence posts, repeated houses.

Coordinates are integer block positions in the build (Y up; north = -Z, south = +Z, east = +X, west = -X). Regions are inclusive boxes between two corners given in any order. Blocks are Java Edition blockstates ("minecraft:oak_planks", "minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=east,half=top]"); the namespace is optional, omitted properties take their defaults, unknown blocks or properties are rejected with suggestions.

Examples:
- Window repeated 4 times, every 3 blocks along X: {"region":{"from":{"x":1,"y":2,"z":0},"to":{"x":1,"y":3,"z":0}},"to":{"x":4,"y":2,"z":0},"repeat":4,"step":{"x":3,"y":0,"z":0}}

from.description: Block position, integers in [-4096, 4096]. Y is up; north = -Z, south = +Z, east = +X, west = -X.

to.description: Block position, integers in [-4096, 4096]. Y is up; north = -Z, south = +Z, east = +X, west = -X.
Destination of the source's minimum corner (first copy).

step.description: Offset between consecutive copies. Default: {x: source size along X, y: 0, z: 0}.

tools.name: insert_module
tools.description:
Inserts a tested module (redstone circuits such as doors, clocks or farms, and prefabricated parts) from the module catalogue. pos is the module's documented anchor, facing its orientation; params are module-specific name/value pairs. Redstone must only be built with this tool. An unknown moduleId is rejected with the list of available modules.

Coordinates are integer block positions in the build (Y up; north = -Z, south = +Z, east = +X, west = -X). Regions are inclusive boxes between two corners given in any order. Blocks are Java Edition blockstates ("minecraft:oak_planks", "minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=east,half=top]"); the namespace is optional, omitted properties take their defaults, unknown blocks or properties are rejected with suggestions.

Examples:
- Module facing east with one parameter: {"moduleId":"piston_door_2x2","pos":{"x":5,"y":1,"z":0},"facing":"east","params":[{"name":"sticky","value":true}]}

moduleId.description: Id of a module from the module catalogue.

pos.description: Position of the module's documented anchor.

params.description: Module-specific parameters as name/value pairs (names must be unique). At most 32 items.
